coverage.limitations: Partial text projection: unsupported blocks may contain additional prose or media. Assessment correctness and scoring reflect authored source and course/lesson defaults, not workspace settings; open or unsupported correctness stays unknown. Media sources and asset status are known, but remote contents, caption-track prose, and audio/video playback lengths are not measured. Stored narration durations are sidecar-recorded alignment endpoints, not measured full-file durations; narration time remains a script estimate at 150 words per minute. Disabled and unlinked scripts are excluded from spoken counts. Feedback, glossary definitions, media alternatives and authored transcripts are separate from on-screen prose. Reading and course timing omit unprojected content and media playback.

trace.see: Objectives stated but never practised or checked
trace.could: The objective may be assessed elsewhere in a larger programme, or the course may not yet give learners a chance to show it.

trace.see: Long stretches of instruction with no activity or check
trace.could: A deliberate reading phase, or a place where learners go long without doing anything with what they read.

trace.see: New concepts bunched on a few pages
trace.could: A glossary or overview page doing its job, or a heavy introduction the learner meets all at once.

anatomy.see: A lesson made almost entirely of text
anatomy.could: A reading or reference lesson, fitting for foundations; worth a second look if its objectives ask learners to do something.

anatomy.see: Explore blocks carrying much of a lesson
anatomy.could: Content the learner can choose to open; well suited to optional depth, riskier for anything a later check needs.

anatomy.see: Activities or checks only at the end of a lesson
anatomy.could: An end-of-lesson assessment design, or practice that could be spread through the lesson.

anatomy.see: Long runs of pages without an activity or check
anatomy.could: A narrative or conceptual stretch, or a place where attention may drift; look at what the learner does next.

tasks.see: A page asks for more than one task type
tasks.could: The learner may combine kinds of work on one page; inspect each quoted request before revising it.
The course states the task, while completion or participation may be recorded elsewhere or remain unseen.
The request may be ambiguous, or inspection may not expose enough text to classify it.

pace.see: Narration much longer than reading time
pace.could: Narration that adds explanation the screen leaves out, or a page learners will skip ahead of.

pace.see: A few pages far longer than their neighbours
pace.could: Dense pages that could be split, or deliberate case studies and summaries.

pace.see: A steep stretch of the running total
pace.could: Where the course takes the most time, which is where changes save learners the most minutes.

evidence.see: An objective group with no check or activity
evidence.could: Knowledge the course introduces but does not ask learners to show, perhaps by design as prior or awareness-level knowledge.

evidence.see: One group with most of the evidence
evidence.could: The course's core outcome, or practice concentrated on what is easiest to check.

flow.see: Checks whose instruction comes after them
flow.could: A pre-test or retrieval-first design, or a check placed before its teaching by mistake.

flow.see: Evidence that traces back to few objectives
flow.could: Objectives that are broad enough to cover much, or objectives the evidence does not reach.

outcomes.see: Objectives mostly at Remember and Understand
outcomes.could: A foundations or awareness course, which may be the intent; check that activities do not ask for more than the objectives state, or less.

outcomes.see: Objectives at Apply or above with only recall checks
outcomes.could: Checks that measure less than the objectives promise.

outcomes.see: Most objectives Verbal information in Gagné's terms
outcomes.could: A course about knowing that; skills learners must perform need practice with feedback, not only statements.

outcomes.see: Objectives that state an action but no conditions or standard
outcomes.could: Common and often fine; a standard is worth adding where the course must show learners reached a level.

availability.could: Content learners may never open; fine for optional depth, a risk when a check depends on it.

availability.see: Needed instruction many minutes before the check
availability.could: Deliberate spacing that strengthens memory, or a gap long enough that learners need a recap first.

availability.see: Needed instruction only in narration or a tooltip
availability.could: Information some learners never see; check that the screen carries it too.
Checks that find out what learners already know; worth asking what the results change, such as letting learners skip ahead or pointing them to the right section.

availability.see: Checks taught only after they are asked, not marked as pre-assessments
availability.could: A retrieval-first or discovery design, or a check placed before its teaching by mistake.
Prior knowledge the course assumes, a scenario judgement that needs none, or a gap in the teaching.

concepts.see: A concept used before it is defined
concepts.could: A preview or advance organiser, or a definition that arrives too late.

concepts.see: Defined concepts with no knowledge check
concepts.could: Supporting ideas that need no check, or core ideas the course never asks learners to use.

concepts.see: A concept that appears once and never returns
concepts.could: A passing mention, or an idea that needs revisiting to be remembered.

prerequisites.see: A concept that comes before what it builds on
prerequisites.could: A spiral design that returns to it later, or an ordering to fix.

spacing.see: Long gaps between encounters with a concept
spacing.could: Spacing that helps long-term memory, or a concept that fades before it is needed; it depends on how long learners must remember it.

spacing.see: Every encounter within a few minutes
spacing.could: Massed practice that feels fluent but fades faster than spaced practice.

distinctions.see: A confusable pair with no stated difference or contrasting example
distinctions.could: A distinction learners already hold, or one they will blur; a side-by-side example is the usual remedy.
Distinctions the course explains but does not ask learners to make.

sentence-length.see: Many sentences past the dashed line
sentence-length.could: Long sentences that load working memory, often lists or qualifications that read better split.

sentence-length.see: Narration sentences longer than on-screen ones
sentence-length.could: Harder to follow by ear than on the page. Where learners can read along, as with the transcript Studio shows beside narrated slides, they can reread and it matters less; it matters most for learners who listen without looking.

readability.see: A lesson with few shared words between sentences
readability.could: Each sentence starts a new thread, as in lists of facts or bullet-like prose; learners must connect the ideas themselves. Fine for reference text, harder for an explanation.

readability.see: Few causal or contrast connectives in an explanatory lesson
readability.could: Reasons and differences left implicit; a because or however can make the logic visible. Procedural steps need fewer.

readability.see: A lesson high on several measures at once
readability.could: Long sentences, rare words and loose connections together are the clearest sign of text worth revising first.

readability.see: A lesson several Flesch–Kincaid grades above the rest
readability.could: Longer sentences or longer words, which is all the formula counts: dense academic-style prose, or subject terms that are long but taught.

structure.see: Clusters of passive or front-loaded sentences
structure.could: Formal or legal source language carried over; the review list shows each sentence.

review.see: The same construction repeating in one lesson
review.could: One writer's habit or one source's style, cheapest to fix together.

longest.see: Lists run together as one sentence
longest.could: Content that would read better as a bulleted list.

vocabulary.see: A lesson with many rare words
vocabulary.could: Subject terminology the course teaches, which is fine when defined, or general wording that could be plainer.

vocabulary.see: Rare words with no glossary tooltip
vocabulary.could: Terms learners may not know; check whether the text explains them nearby.

acronyms.could: Terms the audience already knows, or ones a newcomer cannot decode.

terms.could: A lesson written for a more expert reader than the rest.
Steps in reasoning the writer knows and the learner may not; each flag quotes the words concerned.

emphasis.see: A high share of emphasised words
emphasis.could: Emphasis that no longer stands out; when much is bold, nothing is.

emphasis.see: Emphasis on labels rather than concepts
emphasis.could: Formatting used for layout, which is fine, while key ideas go unmarked.

visuals.could: A page carrying a process or comparison in prose that a diagram would make easier to follow.
